A traditionalist Muslim organisation founded in Surabaya, Java, in 1926. With tens of millions of members it is often called the largest Islamic organisation in the world.

Its founder, the scholar Hasyim Asy'ari, ran a famous pesantren, a rural Islamic boarding school. He and other teachers of the Dutch East Indies felt threatened from two sides. At home the modernist Muhammadiyah attacked local customs as impure. Abroad, the Saudi conquest of Mecca brought the strict teaching of Ibn Abd al-Wahhab to the holy cities.

NU defended the old ways: the classical schools of law, respect for scholars, visits to saints' graves, and local rituals that do not break Islamic law. Its strength lies in thousands of pesantren and village networks, especially in East and Central Java.

It became a political party in the 1950s and stayed a major force. Abdurrahman Wahid, the founder's grandson and a long time NU chairman, served as president of Indonesia from 1999 to 2001. NU now presents itself as a voice for a tolerant Islam rooted in local culture.
sum: A traditionalist Muslim organisation founded in Surabaya, Java, in 1926. With tens of millions of members it is often called the largest Islamic organisation in the world.
